title: A conflict inside a pull request
concept: main moved under your branch; merge main in, resolve, push

story.speaker: Sam
story.text: Bad timing. I changed the same README line you did, and mine is already in main.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: So your pull request cannot merge cleanly. The website says it has a conflict.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: The fix happens on your laptop, not on the website.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Bring main into your branch: `git pull origin main`. That is where the conflict appears.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Fix the file so it keeps both facts, commit, and push. The pull request goes green.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Never clone the project again to escape a conflict. That loses your work.

files.README.md:
The Lantern Labs festival website
Tickets cost 10 dollars.

commit.message: Say tickets are cheaper for students

files.README.md:
The Lantern Labs festival website
Tickets cost 10 dollars, or 6 for students.

The Lantern Labs festival website
Tickets cost 10 dollars. Children go free.

items.text: Bring main's change into your branch and solve the conflict
Keep your own student price too
Push the merged file so the pull request can merge

hints: The conflict is between main and your branch. Pull main into your branch to see it.
Run `git pull origin main`. Git stops with a conflict in README.md. Edit it to keep both sentences, then add and commit.
`git pull origin main`, edit README.md so it mentions students and children, remove the <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>> lines, then `git add README.md`, `git commit`, `git push`.
recap: When main moves under your branch, pull main into your branch, fix the conflict there, and push. The pull request updates itself. Never re-clone to escape a conflict.

cheatSheet.summary: Bring the latest main into the branch you are on

predict.question: Where does the conflict have to be fixed?

choices.text: On the website, in the pull request
On your laptop, then pushed up

predict.explanation: Git needs a human to decide what the file should say. You do that on your laptop and push the answer.
